C-N cross-coupling.description: Forms aryl C-N bonds from aryl halides or triflates and amines, or from arylboronic acids and anilines or NH five-membered heteroarenes.

N-oxide formation.description: Oxidizes azaarene nitrogen to an N-oxide in the encoded ring contexts.

N-protection.description: Installs Boc on aliphatic amines or an enol-ether-derived protecting group on an N-H azole.

abstract carbonyl transformation.description: Adds an O, N, or nH nucleophile to a ketone and forms a heteroatom-substituted tertiary or quaternary carboxylic acid product.

acetal formation.description: Forms acetals or ketals by alcohol addition, carbonyl protection (including cyclic acetals of aromatic aldehydes with vicinal diols), or catechol methylenation.

acid chloride formation.description: Converts a carboxylic acid to an acyl chloride.

acyl activation.description: Converts carboxylic acids, including aromatic acids, to acyl chlorides using an explicit chlorinating reactant such as thionyl chloride.

alcohol halogenation.description: Converts an alcohol or phenol-like OH group to a bromide-bearing carbon product.

alkene C-C coupling.description: Builds substituted alkenes by Heck-type coupling of alkenes with alkyl or aryl bromides or iodides, vinyl-organometallic coupling, or cross metathesis.

alkene formation.description: Forms alkenes by alcohol elimination; use the encoded beta site and check unspecified E/Z geometry.

alkene-forming carbonyl condensation.description: Condenses aldehydes with enolizable carbonyl compounds or activated methyl or methylene partners to form substituted alkenes.

alkene-forming carbonyl transformation.description: Converts an aldehyde or ketone and a haloalkyl partner into an alkene product at the former carbonyl carbon.

alkyne C-C coupling.description: Forms alkyl- or aryl-alkynyl bonds by Sonogashira-type coupling of terminal alkynes with alkyl or aryl halides (vinyl halides do not match), or by a specific net alkyne-exchange rule.

alkyne carbonyl formation.description: Couples a terminal alkyne with an acyl halide or aldehyde-like carbonyl halide partner to form an alkynyl ketone.

alpha halogenation.description: Brominates the alpha position of carbonyl compounds, including carboxylic acids or carboxylates with an alpha C-H and alpha methyl groups with an implicit bromine source.

amide formation.description: Forms amides by acylating amines with acids or O, Cl, N, or S-linked donors; includes hydroxamates, nitrile hydration, ring openings, and selected net multistep rules.

amidine formation.description: Forms amidines or guanidine-like products by substituting imidothioate-like precursors with primary amines, or N-aryl formamidines by condensing anilines with formamide dimethyl acetal.

amidoxime formation.description: Adds hydroxylamine to an aromatic nitrile to form an amidoxime; separate rules encode different tautomers, including C(=NH)-NHOH.

amine alkylation.description: Forms N-C bonds by N-alkylation with halides or mesylates, activated-alcohol coupling, epoxide opening, reductive coupling, or specific net methyl-transfer rules.

amine conjugate addition.description: Adds a primary or secondary amine or an N-H azole to an activated alkene, such as an acrylonitrile, to form a beta-amino electron-withdrawing product.

aromatic amination.description: Forms aryl C-N bonds by replacing aryl fluoride, heteroaryl chloride, or methylsulfinyl substituents with amine or ammonia nitrogen.

aromatic deamination.description: Replaces an aromatic amino group by hydrogen through a net deamination step.

aromatic deoxygenation.description: Removes phenolic or aryl-triflate oxygen substitution to restore aromatic C-H.

aromatic halodeoxygenation.description: Replaces a hydroxyazaarene oxygen substituent with halogen from an explicit donor.

aromatic hydroxylation.description: Converts an aromatic amine to phenol through a net nitrous-acid transformation.

aromatic nitration.description: Replaces aromatic C-H with a nitro group on carbocyclic or azaarene rings, in some rules from explicit nitric acid.

aryl C-C coupling.description: Couples a carboxylated aryl partner with an aryl or heteroaryl halide to form a biaryl C-C bond, representing an abstract decarboxylative or directed cross-coupling.

azo formation.description: Combines nitrous-acid diazotization and aromatic coupling to construct an azo linkage.

benzazole formation.description: Condenses a carboxylic acid or ester-like partner with an ortho amino, hydroxy, thio, or amino arene to form a benzimidazole, benzoxazole, or benzothiazole-like ring.

benzimidazole annulation.description: Closes a benzimidazole ring from an ortho-diamine and an acyl donor, aliphatic carboxylic acid, aldehyde, formic acid, or orthoester.

benzisoxazole annulation.description: Forms fused benzisoxazoles from ortho-fluoro aromatic ketones and hydroxylamine.

benzodiazepinone formation.description: Condenses a 2-aminoaryl ketone or aldehyde with an N-Boc amino acid to form a seven-membered 1,3-dihydro-2H-1,4-benzodiazepin-2-one.

benzofuran formation.description: Combines an alpha-halo electron-withdrawing partner with a salicylaldehyde-like phenol to form a benzofuran ring.

benzothiazole annulation.description: Closes an N-arylthiourea into an aminobenzothiazole through net oxidative C-S bond formation.

borylation.description: Replaces an aryl halide with a boronate or boronic acid using a diboron or trialkyl borate partner, or protects a boronic acid as its pinacol ester.

carbamate annulation.description: Closes amino alcohols into cyclic carbamates with an explicit carbonylating reagent.

carbamate formation.description: Constructs carbamates from amines and O-linked carbonyl donors; some rules encode additional net changes.

carbon-carbon acylation.description: Forms C-C bonds to an acyl carbon by ester enolate acylation, Claisen condensation, aromatic acylation or formylation, or Stetter-type conjugate acylation.

carbon-carbon addition.description: Adds carbon donors to carbonyls, imines, or fulvenes, including net aryl-bromide metalation and ketone addition; organometallic preparation is implicit.

carbon-carbon cleavage.description: Removes formyl, carboxyl-derived, or alkyl fragments; inspect mapping carefully for abstract chain-shortening rules.

carbon-carbon coupling.description: Forms C-C bonds by Suzuki (boronic acid or boronate ester) or Sonogashira coupling, enolate alkylation, or other net carbon-transfer rules.

carbon-carbon cross-coupling.description: Couples alkyl, vinyl, alkynyl, or aryl bromides or iodides with each other, or aryl halides with alkylmagnesium, alkylzinc, or methylboroxine partners, to form a C-C bond.

carbon-carbon rearrangement.description: Rearranges allyl aryl ethers to ortho-allylated phenols, or performs a specific organopotassium/azaarene skeletal rearrangement with extensive ring-atom reorganization.

carbonyl addition.description: Adds an organohalide-derived carbon group to an aldehyde or ketone to form an alcohol product.

carbonyl formation.description: Forms ketones from a nitrile and an organohalide-like partner (an abstract nitrile acylation), or unmasks a ketone by net cleavage of a methyl enol ether.

carbonyl transformation.description: Adds or condenses an activated methylene compound with an activated carbamate-like electrophile to form a substituted carbonyl amide product.

carboxylation.description: Installs an aromatic carboxylic acid using explicit carbon dioxide; activation and regioselectivity remain implicit.

cyclic anhydride formation.description: Cyclodehydrates adjacent aromatic carboxylic acids into a cyclic anhydride.

cyclic peptide formation.description: Cyclizes an amino ester with a protected amino acid partner to form a diketopiperazine-like cyclic diamide.

cyclic urea formation.description: Combines a primary amine and a beta-amino ester with an implicit carbonyl source to form a 3-substituted dihydrouracil (1,3-diazinane-2,4-dione).

cyclic urea or imide formation.description: Cyclizes an amino ester-like reactant with an amine to form an imidazolidinedione or hydantoin-like cyclic urea product.

cycloaddition.description: Combines a diene and alkene dienophile to form a cyclohexene ring through a [4+2] cycloaddition.

cyclopropane formation.description: Closes a cyclopropane by net dialkylation of an activated methylene with dibromoethane, or by a highly abstract closure between two methyl groups on the same carbon.

dehydrogenation.description: Forms alkenes or aromatic heterocycles by net hydrogen removal from the specified saturated substrate.

deprotection.description: Removes Boc, Cbz, benzyl, trityl, THP, silyl, alkyl ether, acetal, acetonide, acyl, or phthalimide protecting groups from N or O; each rule has a specific substrate scope.

diazepine annulation.description: Encodes Boc removal followed by intramolecular condensation to a fused diazepine.

diazine annulation.description: Condenses a substituted hydrazine with an extended dicarbonyl chain to form a six-membered diazine or dihydrodiazine ring, or glyoxal with an ortho aromatic diamine to form a quinoxaline.

enamine formation.description: Forms enamines by replacing the ethoxy group of an ethyl vinyl ether with a primary amine (alkyl, aryl, or acylhydrazide NH2; no activating group is required on the alkene), or by combining a beta-ketoester, propiolate, and primary amine into an unsaturated beta-enamino diester.

enamine or alkene formation.description: Condenses a beta-dicarbonyl compound, a trimethyl or triethyl orthoester, and a primary amine to form a 2-(aminoalkylidene)-1,3-dicarbonyl enamine. The orthoester carbon must carry a carbon substituent, so orthoformates do not match.

epoxidation.description: Transfers oxygen from an explicit peroxide or peracid to an alkene, forming an epoxide.

epoxide opening.description: Opens epoxides with primary alkylamines, ammonia, secondary amines, or N-H azoles to form beta-amino alcohols.

ester formation.description: Forms esters by alcohol acylation, including acetylation with anhydrides and condensation with aliphatic acids, or by carboxylate alkylation.

ester hydrolysis.description: Converts methyl, ethyl, tert-butyl, and other encoded alkyl esters to carboxylic acids.

ether formation.description: Forms ethers by O-alkylation, aromatic substitution, alcohol coupling, epoxide opening, oxa-Michael addition, isobutene addition, or diazocarbonyl O-H insertion.

ether or thioether formation.description: Couples an alcohol, phenol, or thiol with an organic halide to form an ether or thioether C-O/C-S bond. The halide carbon may be alkyl, aryl, or vinyl, so aryl ether formation also matches; acyl halides are excluded.

fused heteroaromatic annulation.description: Forms fused heteroaromatic rings from ortho-functionalized aryl or heteroaryl halides and terminal alkynes, or fused pyrazolopyrimidines by condensing aminopyrazole-like partners with beta-diketones.

fused heterocycle annulation.description: Cyclizes a nitrile-containing carbon partner with an anthranilate-like amine ester to form a fused nitrogen heterocycle.

fused imidazole annulation.description: Forms a fused imidazole from an amino azaarene and an alpha-bromo aromatic ketone.

fused triazine formation.description: Condenses an aminobenzonitrile-like arene with an aliphatic amine to form a fused nitrogen-rich heteroaromatic ring.

guanidine formation.description: Forms guanidines by aniline guanylation, by displacing methylthio from isothiourea-like donors with primary alkylamines, or by an abstract three-amine net transformation.

halogen exchange.description: Exchanges chloride for iodide on primary alkyl substrates, aryl chloride for fluoride, or alkyl mesylate for iodide, using an explicit hydrogen halide where encoded.

halogenation.description: Introduces halogen at aromatic, heteroaromatic, benzylic, or aliphatic C-H sites, or by replacing alcohol, amino, or lactam groups; activation and selectivity are rule-specific.

heteroaromatic annulation.description: Condenses an ortho-amino aryl carbonyl partner with an enolizable carbonyl compound to form a quinoline-like heteroaromatic ring.

heteroatom substitution.description: Replaces carbon-bound leaving groups with heteroatom donors; broad queries need activation and valence checks.

heterocycle annulation.description: Combines an isothiocyanate, an alpha-halo carbonyl compound, and a primary amine to form an imino-substituted thiazole ring.

heterocycle condensation.description: Condenses an isothiocyanate-derived component with an aryl aldehyde to form a thiazolidinone or rhodanine-like alkene product.

hydrazine formation.description: Encodes the net multistage conversion of an aniline to an arylhydrazine; diazotization and reduction conditions are implicit.

hydrostannylation.description: Adds a trialkyltin hydride across a terminal alkyne to give a vinylstannane.

imidazole formation.description: Cyclizes an alpha-bromoketone with an amidine-like partner to form a substituted imidazole ring.

imide or bis-amide formation.description: Acylates amines with bifunctional acyl donors, such as phthalic anhydride with primary alkylamines, to form imides or bis-amides.

imidoyl halide formation.description: Chlorinates an aldimine carbon using an explicit chlorine donor while retaining the C=N bond.

imine or hydrazone formation.description: Condenses an alkyl hydrazine with an aldehyde to form a hydrazone C=N bond.

indazole annulation.description: Forms indazoles from ortho-fluoro aromatic nitriles and a nitrogen partner (aminoindazoles), or from ortho-toluidine and nitrous acid.

indole annulation.description: Forms indoles through Fischer arylhydrazine-carbonyl annulation or ortho-haloaniline-alkyne coupling and cyclization.

isothiazole annulation.description: Builds a cyanoisothiazole through the specific dithiazole/enamine ring transformation encoded in the template.

lactam annulation.description: Forms isoindolinone, benzoxazinone, acridone-like, or piperidinone rings by intramolecular acylation or azadiene cycloaddition.

lactam chlorodehydration.description: Converts an aromatic lactam tautomer into a chloroazaarene using explicit phosphorus oxychloride.

lactam formation.description: Cyclizes a primary amine with an unsaturated dicarbonyl carboxylic acid to form a substituted lactam or pyrrolidinone-like ring.

multicomponent heterocycle annulation.description: Combines a urea-like or other nitrogen donor, an aryl aldehyde, and a beta-ketoester-like carbonyl component to form dihydropyrimidinone or aminodihydropyridine rings.

nitrile formation.description: Forms nitriles by halide substitution (including CuCN substitution of aryl bromides), primary amide dehydration, or net alcohol or amine conversions.

nitrile hydrolysis.description: Converts nitriles to carboxylic acids in net graph rules requiring explicit alcohol and water reactants; inspect atom-source roles.

nitrogen heterocycle annulation.description: Forms purine- or triazine-like fused nitrogen heterocycles from two primary amines through implicit carbon and nitrogen atoms, or performs other specific nitrogen-ring closures and skeletal edits.

olefination.description: Replaces carbonyl oxygen with a carbon fragment, including phosphonium olefination of aromatic aldehydes to terminal alkenes and unusual net methylenation rules.

oxadiazole annulation.description: Forms oxadiazole or oxadiazolone rings from amidoxime, acylhydrazine, nitrile, or cyanamide partners, including 1,2,4-oxadiazoles from aromatic acids and aromatic amidoximes.

oxadiazole formation.description: Combines a nitrile-containing partner with a carboxylic acid to form an oxadiazole-like five-membered heteroaromatic ring.

oxadiazole or thiadiazole formation.description: Condenses a hydrazide-like precursor with an isothiocyanate to form an oxadiazole-like heteroaromatic product bearing an amino substituent.

oxalamide formation.description: Couples two amines through an implicit oxalyl carbonyl linker to form an oxalamide N-C(=O)-C(=O)-N motif.

oxazoline annulation.description: Constructs an oxazoline from an isocyanoacetamide and aldehyde; inspect template-imposed stereochemistry.

oxidation.description: Oxidizes primary alcohols to aldehydes and secondary alcohols to ketones, and covers benzylic oxidation, alpha hydroxylation, quinone formation, and Baeyer-Villiger oxygen insertion.

oxidative cleavage.description: Cleaves the encoded terminal alkenes to carbonyl products; check the exact product components.

oxime formation.description: Condenses hydroxylamine or O-substituted hydroxylamines with aromatic aldehydes or aryl alkyl ketones to form oximes or oxime ethers.

oxygen heterocycle annulation.description: Forms fused oxygen heterocycles, such as chromanones from ortho-hydroxy aryl ketones and cyclic ketones, or benzofuranones from mandelic-acid and phenol fragments.

phosphonate chemistry.description: Forms C-P phosphonates by Arbuzov transformations or removes phosphonate ester protection.

phosphonium formation.description: Forms phosphonium salts or carbonyl-stabilized phosphoranes used as olefination precursors.

phthalazinone formation.description: Condenses a monosubstituted hydrazine with a 2-formylaryl methyl ester to form a 2-substituted phthalazin-1(2H)-one.

protecting group removal.description: Removes a tert-butoxycarbonyl protecting group from an amine to reveal the free amine.

pyrazole annulation.description: Forms pyrazole from a specific heteroaryl enaminone and arylhydrazine; the N-atom mapping is uncertain.

pyrazole formation.description: Condenses a substituted hydrazine with a 1,3-dicarbonyl-like compound to form a pyrazole ring.

pyrrole annulation.description: Forms N-arylpyrroles from anilines and either 1,4-diketone or masked 1,4-dicarbonyl partners.

pyrrole formation.description: Condenses a 1,4-dicarbonyl-like chain with a primary amine to form a pyrrole ring.

quinazolinone formation.description: Cyclizes an ortho-amino benzamide-like reactant with a carbonyl compound to form a quinazolinone-like ring.

quinolone annulation.description: Closes an ortho-fluoroaryl enaminone into a quinolone through intramolecular substitution.

reduction.description: Reduces nitro, azide, nitrile, carbonyl, imine, acid, ester, amide, alkene, alkyne, aromatic, indole, or silicon-halide groups; each rule encodes a specific substrate pattern.

reductive amination.description: Couples aldehydes or ketones, including formaldehyde (methylation), azetidinone, and oxetanone, with amines by net reductive amination.

reductive dehalogenation.description: Replaces aromatic or heteroaromatic halogen substituents with hydrogen; reagent and site selectivity are implicit.

saturated heterocycle annulation.description: Forms saturated heterocycles, such as fused nitrogen rings from amino arylalkyl precursors and aldehydes, or six-membered N/P rings by primary-amine double addition to divinyl phosphorus.

silyl protection.description: Converts alcohols to silyl ethers using alkyl- or aryl-substituted chlorosilanes.

sulfonamide annulation.description: Cyclizes an amine with an aryl sulfonyl chloride bearing an ester-like group to form a cyclic sulfonamide or sultam-like product.

sulfonamide formation.description: Forms sulfonamides by N-sulfonylation of amines, anilines, or azoles with sulfonyl halides, including vinyl sulfonamides by sulfonylation with chloroethyl elimination.

sulfonate formation.description: Converts alcohols or phenols to sulfonate esters, including mesylates, arylsulfonates, and triflates.

sulfone formation.description: Forms a sulfone C-S(=O)2-C linkage from two carbon leaving-group partners with an implicit sulfur dioxide equivalent.

sulfonyl chloride formation.description: Forms sulfonyl chlorides by sulfonic-acid activation or aromatic chlorosulfonylation.

sulfoxide formation.description: Forms sulfoxides by coupling a thiol-like sulfur nucleophile with a carbon leaving-group partner, or by oxidizing an aryl methyl sulfide with explicit hydrogen peroxide.

sulfur oxidation.description: Oxidizes the encoded thioethers to sulfoxides or sulfones; choose the rule for the intended oxidation state.

suzuki cross-coupling.description: Couples aryl or heteroaryl boronic acids with aryl or heteroaryl halides or triflates to form biaryl C-C bonds.

tetrazole annulation.description: Forms tetrazoles by cycloaddition of an explicit azide to a nitrile, giving the encoded neutral tetrazole tautomer.

tetrazole formation.description: Converts a nitrile into a tetrazole ring using an implicit azide source.

thiazole annulation.description: Condenses thiourea with an alpha-chloro aliphatic ketone to form an aminothiazole.

thiazole formation.description: Converts an alpha-halo carbonyl compound into a 2-aminothiazole (Hantzsch-type); the ring sulfur, ring nitrogen, C2, and amino nitrogen come from an implicit thiourea.

thioether formation.description: Forms thioether C-S-C linkages from two organic halides with an implicit sulfur source, or aryl or heteroaryl sulfides from thiols or dimethyl disulfide and halide partners.

thionation.description: Replaces amide or aromatic lactam carbonyl oxygen with sulfur using explicit Lawesson's reagent or phosphorus pentasulfide.

thiourea formation.description: Couples an isothiocyanate with a primary or secondary amine to form a thiourea C(=S)-N product.

triazole annulation.description: Forms triazole rings by alkyne-azide cycloaddition of alkyl azides with terminal alkynes, or by hydrazino-azaarene condensation with an orthoester.

triazole formation.description: Combines an isothiocyanate, amine, and hydrazide-like component to form an amino-substituted triazole-like heteroaromatic ring.

triazole functionalization.description: Combines an organic azide and a primary amine with an implicit three-carbon propargyl unit (the CH2 linker and both triazole carbons) to form a 1-substituted 4-(aminomethyl)-1,2,3-triazole, as in N-propargylation followed by azide-alkyne cycloaddition.

urea formation.description: Forms ureas from amines and isocyanates (including aryl isocyanates) or carbamates, plus an abstract two-amine net rule.

urea or carbamate transformation.description: Couples an alpha-amino ester with an N-substituted 2,2,2-trifluoroethyl carbamate (an activated carbamate, not a protected amino acid) to form an N,N'-disubstituted urea, with the ester hydrolysed to the carboxylic acid.
